Principle among them is taking a drag where the fume concentration is too high, which brings the lit cigarette to several times the temperature needed to ignite gasoline. Dropping ash too close to spilled gasoline (but not in it) can also cause an ignition, as the fall aerates it and the impact throws small high temperature embers short distances ("sparks") -- as opposed to throwing the whole thing or a butt where the unlit higher mass end almost always goes first, shielding the combustion from the wind, and impacts first, limiting the "sparking".
